name: MITRE D3FEND™
purpose: A common vocabulary for defensive techniques, tied to the attacker techniques they answer.
what: D3FEND 1.6.0 is a knowledge graph of countermeasures under seven tactics: Model, Harden, Detect, Isolate, Deceive, Evict and Restore.

binds.line: Nobody is bound by it, and nothing is audited against it.

verifiedBy.line: D3FEND says it ‘does not prescribe specific countermeasures, it does not prioritize them, and it does not characterize their effectiveness’.

sits.line: Beside the stack, in the adversary column: the defender’s half of the same map.

sources.title: D3FEND: A Knowledge Graph of Cybersecurity Countermeasures

verification.note: Read on 14 November 2026. Version 1.6.0 is dated 31 August 2026. The matrix has seven tactics. The site prints no total of techniques: 271 is a count, made that day, of the entries in D3FEND’s own technique list (https://d3fend.mitre.org/api/technique/all.json). Release 1.6.0 tracks ATT&CK v19.0, not v20.
Read on 14 November 2026: ‘D3FEND is a knowledge base, but more specifically a knowledge graph, of cybersecurity countermeasure techniques’, and the sentence quoted on this card.

terms.line: Used under MITRE’s D3FEND Terms of Use, whose license has the same form as ATT&CK’s. This round shows the card. MITRE D3FEND™ is a trademark of The MITRE Corporation.

related.line: Each countermeasure is tied to the ATT&CK techniques it answers.
A control says what must be done; D3FEND names the technique that does it.
